question: Was 80 Pioneer Street in Red Hook inside the area Hurricane Sandy flooded in 2012?

plan.rationale: The query specifies a single street address ('80 Pioneer Street') and asks about its exposure to Hurricane Sandy's flood zone in 2012.

claims.text: This address is mapped within the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) and is modeled to be in FEMA flood zone AE (a Special Flood Hazard Area), per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970192F, effective 2007.
USGS recorded one Hurricane Ida high-water mark within 800 meters of this address, with the highest observed water elevation at 4.2 feet, up to 0.3 feet above ground.
Experimental: Satellite-detected surface water about 14 hours after Hurricane Ida showed no water polygons within 500 meters of this address, with the nearest water 4017.7 meters away.
Six FloodNet community sensors within 600 meters have logged nine above-curb flood events in the last three years, with a peak depth recorded of 89 millimeters.
Sixty NYC 311 flood-related complaints have been filed within 200 meters of this location in the last five years, with the most common descriptor being Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments).
The latest NOAA tide reading at The Battery is 5.33 feet above mean lower low water, observed on 2026-09-26 at 18:18, which is 2.13 feet higher than the predicted tide.

NPCC4 projects a median sea-level rise of 0.38 meters (15 inches) by the 2050s and 0.79 meters (31 inches) by 2100 at the Battery, with a 90th percentile of 0.74 meters and 1.65 meters.
